A rare genetic mutation called pseudo-melanism has resulted in roughly half of the tigers in India's Similipal Tiger Reserve sporting coats with far more black than those of usual tigers. This widespread coloration is a symptom of a shallow gene pool in a region that previously faced a dwindling tiger population, and could prove catastrophic if conservation officers aren't able to find these tigers more genetically diverse mates. Native primarily to the snowy boreal forests of the Russian Far East and parts of northeastern China, adult males can grow up to 10–12 feet in length and weigh over 600 pounds, while females are noticeably smaller.
